correctness.rationale: For each k on the three-cycle there is one square atom C and a reversed mixed pair A,B, so the coefficient is Hermitian and equals C^2+AB+BA. Independently, the isometry Vv=(A^(1/2)v,B^(1/2)v,C^(1/2)v) and D=diag(I,-I,0) give X=V*DV=A−B and S=V*D^2V=I−C. Hence S−X^2=W*W with W=(I−VV*)DV. This proves the contraction inequality even for singular effects. Completing the square gives C^2+AB+BA+I/24=W*W/2+3(C−I/6)^2/2. At a contact unit vector v, Cv=v/6, X^2v=5v/6 and Wv=0. The third component of DVv=VXv gives C^(1/2)Xv=0, so w=Xv/sqrt(5/6) is a unit vector in ker C orthogonal to v. On (w,v), X exchanges the basis vectors with coefficient sqrt(5/6) and C is diag(0,1/6); self-adjointness makes this a common reducing block for A,B,C. Substitution gives the exact matrices in the finding and spectrum {1/12,−1/24} for the coefficient. The two rank-one matrices there have determinant zero and positive trace; the block extends by any normalized positive triple and can be placed at any specified k by relabeling the atoms. In dimension one all products are scalar nonnegative; with two group elements B=I−A, so A^2+B^2 and 2A(I−A) are positive. This proves both minimalities. The proof neither assumes invertibility nor depends on sampling.
residual_risks: The equality classification is for one specified coefficient, not a prescribed full convolution spectrum or an extremum over groups of arbitrary order.

value.rationale: This quantifies rather than merely demonstrates failure of convolution positivity in the smallest possible normalized matrix setting. The dimension-free bound is exactly attained, and identifying the forced common reducing block describes all equality cases, not just a numerical minimum or isolated example. That structure is the reason the result goes beyond a routine compression inequality.
residual_risks: The result addresses ordered square convolution on the three-cycle only; it does not bound a general product of matrix-valued measures.
